clue.text: Happy place for Hillary?

definitions.meaning: elated, overjoyed, in the idiom of being on a high
Sir Edmund Hillary first climbed Everest, the summit of the globe

explanation.surface: A question about where the famous mountaineer felt contented.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for elation and also literally describes standing on Everest's summit, where Hillary stood in 1953.

clue.text: Is 12.5% too much alcohol?

definitions.meaning: 12.5 per cent is one eighth, a fraction written as one over eight
slightly drunk, having had a drink more than the limit

explanation.surface: Asks whether wine at 12.5 per cent strength is excessively boozy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mildly tipsy; read literally as a fraction it is one eighth, which is 12.5 per cent.

clue.text: He may repair the floor where line of girl dancers tumbles

indicators.note: the line falls out of the troupe's name, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the Tiller Girls were a famous British precision dance troupe

explanation.surface: A craftsman fixing a stage floor where a chorus line has taken a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a long-running British high-kicking dance troupe; one of their L's 'tumbles' out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays or mends tiles on a floor is a natural candidate for repairing it.

clue.text: The first Greek woman to criticize another

parts.note: to pan a play is to criticize it harshly
another woman, here any girl's name such as Dora

explanation.surface: A Greek woman being the first to find fault with a fellow woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows 'woman' from the definition: another woman, DORA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Pandora was the first mortal woman, fashioned by the gods and given the fateful jar.

clue.text: Pots of nice stew eaten by ancient fairyfolk

indicators.note: being eaten means going inside the fairyfolk word

parts.note: fae is an old word for the fairy people

indicators.note: a stew mixes its contents, so the letters of nice are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pots of tasty stew devoured by the fairies of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the food in the pots, but it is the anagram signal; fae is an archaic word for fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is glazed earthenware, so pots and other vessels made of it are collectively so called.

clue.text: Sound of footstep — and the final drop?

definitions.meaning: the click of the back of a shoe hitting the ground
the last bit of liquor left in the bottom of a glass

explanation.surface: A footstep is heard, then a question about a last fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel striking the floor makes a tap; separately the word names the dregs remaining in a drinker's glass.

clue.text: Send out the inexperienced for call-up in 1914, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue, calling the letters up means reading them from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out
raw recruits are the inexperienced

explanation.surface: Sending green recruits off to the front when conscription began in 1914.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call-up' looks like conscription, part of the scene, but signals that EMIT and RAW are read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: 1914 began the Great War, so it is an example of a period of armed conflict.

clue.text: Set irregular pattern for internal security in managed millennium building

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: the security letters sit inside the building

parts.note: the Millennium Dome in London, built for the year 2000
IS abbreviates internal security

explanation.surface: Planning a random security pattern inside a managed millennium building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome is the large London exhibition building opened for the year 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: To randomise is to arrange things haphazardly, giving them a deliberately irregular order.

clue.text: Lovers, holding hands, pace about with no end of rejoicing …

indicators.note: moved about, the letters are shuffled into a new order
the final letter of rejoicing is taken away from holding
the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Lovers hand in hand stroll around, celebrating without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of rejoicing' removes G (the last letter of 'rejoicing') from HOLDING; HOLDIN plus HANDS and PACE is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The shepherd and shepherdess of Longus's Greek romance are a famous pair of young lovers.

clue.text: Retrain inelegant plant

indicators.note: training again rearranges the letters of inelegant

explanation.surface: Training a clumsy-looking shrub into better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is sweetbriar, a wild rose, so it is a kind of flowering shrub.

clue.text: Swiftly make an approach

definitions.meaning: to ... a dress is to sew it quickly
the run before a jump or a delivery in cricket, or the build-up to an event

explanation.surface: Moving fast to approach someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to make quickly, and the hyphenated noun means a preparatory approach or lead-in.

clue.text: "September's child's a-roving, a-roving"

indicators.note: the repeated roving tells the letters of the first a-roving to wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A sea-shanty line about a September baby who loves to wander.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the shanty 'A-Roving' and the rhyme 'Monday's child'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in early or mid September has the star sign of the Virgin, so is a native of that sign.

clue.text: Queen and Empress infinitely old-fashioned when wearing that headgear

indicators.note: the word that is worn around the royal letters like a garment

parts.note: taken as written and split around the middle
R for Regina, Latin for queen
I for Imperatrix, as in Victoria R I

indicators.note: without end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: corny means hackneyed or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Victoria, queen and empress, wearing a quaint hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria signed as R I, Regina Imperatrix. 'infinitely' drops the last letter; 'wearing' splits the word that around the royal letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-cornered hat with its brim turned up is an item of headwear from the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Nearly burn the tea

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch

explanation.surface: Almost scorching the tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is a slang word for tea, taken from the Chinese.

clue.text: Renew hiring for film, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to lease again, renewing a rental agreement
a newly issued film or record is a new issue to the public

explanation.surface: Renting the equipment again for a movie shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it means lease anew; unhyphenated it is a newly issued film, an example of the sense.

clue.text: … and student paces about among the scenery

parts.note: L is the learner plate letter, for a student driver

indicators.note: moved about, the letters of paces are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the lovers' stroll: a student also walking around amid the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 8 Down. 'about' turns PACES into SCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is an expanse of country seen as a view, so it is natural scenery.

clue.text: Meet in city

definitions.meaning: to ... a person is to meet them
a bishop's seat, a cathedral city

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet up in town.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to visit or encounter someone; the noun is a diocese or its cathedral city.

clue.text: Criticism gives writer twitches

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
tics are nervous twitches

explanation.surface: Harsh reviews make an author nervously twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetics is the theory and critical study of poetry, a branch of literary criticism.

clue.text: Some modern poetry

indicators.note: some of the word, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A sample of contemporary verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, so it is a piece of verse.

clue.text: It's hard with company to be remote

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
and joins things together, like with
a set is a group or company of people

explanation.surface: How difficult it is to be distant when among other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset is a hand-held controller, such as the remote for a television.

clue.text: Actor in brief send-up for detergent?

indicators.note: the actor sits inside the shortened send-up
cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a spoof is a send-up or parody
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A performer appearing in a short parody advertisement for washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims SPOOF to SPOO, which holds HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a cleaning agent for hair or carpets, so loosely a kind of detergent, hence the query.

clue.text: Note about earth-shattering drama

indicators.note: the note goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: smashed to pieces, the letters of earth are rearranged

explanation.surface: A review of an earth-shattering stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth-shattering' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen hides the fodder and its anagram signal; te is the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre denotes plays and dramatic art collectively, so it is a synonym for drama.

clue.text: "On The Beach" is where to spot this nameless film star

definitions.text: "On The Beach" is where to spot this

indicators.note: without a name, so N, the abbreviation for name, is removed

parts.note: Sean Bean is an English film actor

explanation.surface: A film star is spotted on the beach, echoing the title of the film On the Beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Bean is an English actor; N for name drops out. 'On The Beach' looks like the movie title.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea beans are large drift seeds washed ashore, so they are found on beaches by beachcombers.

clue.text: Groups worked up about Mandela's party policies

indicators.note: the reversed groups go around the party letters
in a down clue, worked upwards means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: sets are groups
the ANC, African National Congress, led by Nelson Mandela

explanation.surface: Factions agitated over the political programme of Mandela's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked up' looks like agitation, but in this down light it reads the groups word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or attitude adopted on an issue, close to a policy.

clue.text: To the French, names initially appear hard — like this girl's?

definitions.note: the girl's name, which the clue builds

parts.note: à la is French for to the
NN is the plural abbreviation of name

indicators.note: only the opening letter of appear is taken

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: In French, initial names look tough, like a particular girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A from 'appear'. The definition is the girl's name, an Irish endearment meaning my child.
explanation.definitionFit: Alannah is an Irish girl's given name, from a term of endearment for a child.

clue.text: See 12
Navy leaves unexpectedly to put down …

indicators.note: the letters turn up in an unforeseen order

explanation.surface: Sailors suddenly go ashore to suppress a rebellion, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to 26 Across, which supplies the revolt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave is to subjugate people, to put them down by force.

clue.text: … beginnings of armed revolt on island without extremes of language

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two following words
the island name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Jamaica, the Caribbean island

explanation.surface: An armed uprising starting on an island, following the navy of the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without extremes of' removes the J and final A from JAMAICA, leaving AMAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, spoken in the Near East in biblical times.

clue.text: Regularly carsick over time going to the races

indicators.note: every other letter, taken at regular intervals

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A queasy traveller repeatedly sick on the trip to a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is the famous Berkshire racecourse holding Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is an English horse-racing venue, so 'the races' there is a day out at it.

clue.text: Understanding oddities of German spelling

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: Getting the hang of the quirks of German orthography.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a grasp of a subject is to comprehend it well, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Specialised sleuth given bit of change in USA, we hear

indicators.note: the words heard spoken give the answer

parts.words: sleuth given bit of change in USA
parts.note: tec is a detective, and a nickel is a five-cent coin in America

explanation.surface: A private eye handed a coin in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical describes something requiring expert or specialist knowledge in a particular field.

clue.text: Internee has better treatment when chasing the authorities

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so these pieces follow the word the

parts.note: a POW, prisoner of war, is an internee

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A detained prisoner being treated better while pursuing those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges HAS BETTER into ERSTHATBE; 'the' is part of the answer, leaving 'authorities' as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for those holding power or the establishment in charge.
